 Do you have TRICARE For Life ? You should know that the annual Medicare Open Enrollment period runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7. Now is the time to think about making any changes to your Medicare coverage. If you do make changes, they’ll take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
 “Not all TFL beneficiaries will want to make changes to their Medicare coverage during Medicare Open Enrollment period,” said Anne Breslin, TFL Program Manager, TRICARE Health Plan, at the Defense Health Agency. “But there are a few coverage decisions worth considering.”
 It’s important to know that the Medicare Open Enrollment period isn’t the same as the TRICARE Open Season . You don’t need to take any action during TRICARE Open Season to keep your TFL coverage.
 Note: Did you miss your opportunity to sign up for Medicare Part A and Part B during your Initial Enrollment Period? If so, you can sign up during the annual General Enrollment Period , which runs from Jan. 1 to March 31.
 What can I change during Medicare Open Enrollment? 
 Medicare Part D prescription coverage 
 TFL beneficiaries remain eligible for TRICARE prescription drug coverage through the TRICARE Pharmacy Program , as described in the TRICARE For Life Handbook . You aren’t required to have Medicare Part D to have TRICARE prescription drug coverage.
 But in some cases, you may benefit from enrolling in a Part D plan in addition to having TRICARE prescription drug coverage. Here are some things to consider before you enroll in Medicare Part D:
 Drug coverage: Some Medicare Part D plans may cover drugs, such as weight loss drugs, that the TRICARE Pharmacy Program doesn’t cover. Each Medicare Part D plan has its own formulary. Enter your prescription drugs on Medicare’s plan comparison page and compare drug coverage of each Medicare Part D plan with https://www.express-scripts.com/frontend/open-enrollment/tricare/fst/.
 Costs: Each Medicare Part D plan has different monthly premiums, deductibles, and copayments. Compare costs across Medicare Part D plans and TRICARE Pharmacy Program costs .
 Change to or from a Medicare Advantage (Part C) plan 
 Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans are offered by private insurance companies that Medicare approved. These plans provide your Medicare Part A and Part B benefits. Some Medicare Advantage plans include Part D prescription drug coverage.
 You don’t need a Medicare Advantage plan to keep your TFL coverage. If you choose to enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan, you can still use your TFL benefit. Each Medicare Advantage plan has different costs, benefits, and rules. Before enrolling, contact the plan to learn how it works with TFL.
 Get advice and keep your records up to date 
 Have questions about your TFL coverage? You can speak with a Beneficiary Counseling and Assistance Coordinator before making the decision to enroll or make changes to your Medicare coverage. If you do make changes, the TFL contractor or overseas contractor needs to know about any other health insurance. This will help ensure proper coordination of benefits.
 To help ensure your claims process correctly, you should:
 Present all health insurance coverage cards along with your Uniform Services ID card identification card at each medical appointment.
 Keep your information up to date in Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System .
 Inform your TRICARE contractors of your other health insurance . Do this by submitting a completed other health insurance form to the TFL or overseas contractor.
 Where to look for help 
 For more information, check out the TRICARE For Life Handbook . You can also contact your TRICARE contractor for help:
 In the U.S. and U.S. territories: https://tricare4u.com/en/portal/beneficiary/contact-us
 Overseas :https://www.tricare-overseas.com/contact-us
 For TRICARE pharmacy benefit and prescription questions, contact https://militaryrx.express-scripts.com/contact-us.
 TRICARE works closely with Medicare to meet your healthcare needs. It’s a good idea to know your options. Interested in making changes to your Medicare coverage? Visit Medicare.gov before Dec. 7 to learn more.
